title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier plus an automated single-repair iteration into an LLM intent→configuration workflow. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we used shared_initial_candidate semantics: the pipeline produced one shared LLM proposal per task (requested model: gpt-5-mini) that served both as the baseline proposal and as the input to the guarded arm, where a deterministic netops validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) could trigger at most one automated repair call. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; exact McNemar two-sided p (archived executor convention) = 1.00; paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage provider calls = 1. Interpretation: under the tested model, verifier, and verifier-scoped synthetic corpus the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals; the verifier+single-repair corrected one concrete baseline failure but yielded a small measurable pass-rate gain. We document preregistration, precise statistical conventions used, execution accounting, and deterministic artifact-locations so readers can inspect the single corrected episode and all relevant traces in the archived evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configuration, planning multi-step changes, and producing candidate repairs. Systems and reviews emphasize that operational reliability typically depends on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common mitigation is a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) architecture in which a model proposal is checked by a deterministic verifier and repaired or blocked when violations appear. Despite this conceptual consensus, there is little controlled, artifact-backed measurement isolating the verifier’s marginal contribution when the model’s initial proposal is held fixed. Motivated by practical NetOps deployment questions (How much additional safety does a verifier+repair provide if the model’s proposal is unchanged?), we preregistered and executed a paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under canonical, verifier-scoped synthetic workloads.
sections.related_work: Formal and deterministic verification methods for network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, incremental verification) can check reachability, isolation, and update-safety and are widely used as NetOps guardrails [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems report LLM-based intent translators and emphasize the need for validators and operational guardrails [INTA, 2025; Confucius, 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair or critic-in-the-loop patterns have been proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce incorrect outputs and to produce machine-checkable artifacts [PoeTone; INTA]. Failure-mode studies document LLM hallucination, overconfidence, and tool-integration errors, motivating verifier-in-the-loop pipelines [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. However, supplied system papers rarely publish controlled ablations that quantify a verifier’s effect size under reproducible conditions; our work contributes a preregistered, artifact-backed paired measurement focused on one operational semantics (shared_initial_candidate) and one verifier scope (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The confirmatory hypothesis tested whether a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration reduces verifier-detected safety violations relative to the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Multiplicity, missingness, retry, and stopping rules were preregistered and are archived in the execution manifest.

Task corpus and construct control: We generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and stratified allocation: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), static-route-change (166). To ensure construct validity relative to the chosen verifier, tasks were constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}; tasks referencing unmodeled features would have been routed to an 'unmodeled-feature' cohort and excluded per the preregistration (no confirmatory exclusions occurred). Each task contains initial_state, expected_final_state, and an explicit required_sequence; representative task payloads are archived under representative_tasks in the evidence bundle.

Generation semantics and experimental control: The design used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false. For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal (the shared candidate). The baseline condition treated that shared candidate as the model-only proposal. The guarded condition validated the identical shared candidate with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and invoked a single automated repair call only if the validator reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. This semantic isolates the marginal effect of verification and one repair iteration conditional on identical proposals; it intentionally does not measure verifier-guided regeneration or independent guarded-generation strategies.

Models, adapter, and validator: The requested model was gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses). Model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) records max_output_tokens = 2000 and single-attempt generation semantics. The deterministic validator used for pass/fail scoring and repair gating was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator’s specification and the violation-code→severity mapping are archived in the execution bundle.

Confirmatory statistical test: The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the exact McNemar via the discordant-pair binomial: let n = n10 + n01 be the number of discordant pairs and X = n10 the count where guarded==1 and baseline==0 (or equivalently the count in one discordant cell). Under the exact convention, X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5) and the two-sided p-value is computed as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ x_obs), P(X ≥ x_obs)}, truncated at 1.0. For small n this exact-binomial convention is numerically different from the large-sample chi-square approximation; the implementation detail, seed values, and code pointers are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). We report the archived two-sided p and interpret it in the context of observed counts and power assumptions.

Paired-bootstrap CI: We computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute difference with B = 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729. Resampling unit = task/pair with pairing preserved (each resample draws 500 pairs with replacement). The analysis artifacts include bootstrap parameters and resampling code references.

Missingness, retries, and stopping: Up to two automated retries for transient provider errors were permitted per preregistration. The adapter-level model-call budget constrained execution to maximum_model_calls = 1000; the run stopped when the preregistered confirmatory pairs (N = 500) completed. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501, completed_episode_count = 1000, and failed_episode_count = 0.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcome: The experiment completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500 and repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar two-sided p-value and CI: Under the archived exact-binomial discordant-pair convention (n = 1, X = n10 = 1) the two-sided p-value equals p = 1.00 (p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ 1), P(X ≥ 1)} = 2×0.5 = 1.0, truncated at 1.0); this computational rule and its rationale are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.006]. The combination of an extremely low baseline error rate and the small discordant count yields both a near-zero point estimate and a CI compatible with small positive effects up to 0.006 in absolute risk reduction.

Repair activity and discordant-pair provenance: Observed repair-stage calls = 1. That single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1), i.e., it converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. All per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, and the repair prompt/response are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider-call traces. The evidence bundle therefore deterministically supports qualitative inspection of the corrected episode. Because the archive contains the complete raw_results.jsonl and validator traces, the discordant episode is locatable by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pairs where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1; exactly one pair matches this filter in the confirmatory set. The run-level deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) records that stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 500 and repair = 1, and provider_call_audit.hosted_model_call_event_count = 501. Representative per-task exemplar files and provider-call traces are included in the evidence bundle (see artifact_examples and representative_tasks entries).

Secondary and subgroup analyses: Pre-registered secondary analyses by violation class were not informative: observed violation counts were nearly zero, providing no meaningful counts for class-level inference. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline p_b ≈ 0.30; observed baseline prevalence ≈ 0.002 differs materially and produces a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to small absolute improvements. Analysis artifacts (analysis/missingness_summary.csv, analysis/contamination_summary.csv) report no exclusions, no missing pairs, and no contamination events.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: This experiment provides a conditional, artifact-backed measurement of verifier+single-repair impact under a narrowly specified operational regime: one requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), one deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), shared_initial_candidate semantics, and a single automated repair iteration. Under these conditions the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the verifiers corrected one concrete failure, yielding a small absolute pass-rate gain (0.002). Practitioners should therefore interpret this result as a conditional measurement that does not imply verifiers are unnecessary. In workloads with higher baseline error prevalence, broader property coverage, or more heterogeneous vendor CLIs, verifier+repair gains could be substantially larger.

Methodological implications: The shared_initial_candidate semantic isolates the marginal verifier effect given identical proposals; it is appropriate when one must assess the incremental benefit of adding deterministic checks and limited automated repairs to an existing proposal stream without permitting the verifier to steer the model via regeneration. Alternative semantics—verifier-guided regeneration, iterative multi-repair loops, or independent-condition generation—answer different operational questions and can produce different effect sizes. Selection of generation semantics must therefore match the operational objective (minimize final failures vs minimize changed proposals or model calls).

Statistical and power considerations: The preregistered power plan assumed baseline error prevalence ≈ 0.30 and required N ≈ 384 for 80% power to detect a 10 percentage-point absolute reduction. Observed baseline prevalence (~0.002) is far lower, invalidating the power assumptions and producing a ceiling effect: even a verifier that corrected many relative failures could yield only a small absolute risk reduction on the pass-rate metric. The archived paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] and exact-binomial p = 1.00 reflect both the small discordant count and the chosen exact two-sided convention; readers should weigh practical importance (absolute risk reduction) and sample prevalence when interpreting these results.

Reproducibility and artifact-grounded inspection: All preregistration files, task-generator seeds and code, model-configuration, raw LLM responses, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis CSVs are archived in the evidence bundle. Key execution artifact locations and checksums are recorded in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; execution/model_configuration.json; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The single discordant episode can be deterministically located by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pairs where baseline pass == 0 and guarded pass == 1; the filter returns exactly one pair in the confirmatory set and yields the validator violation codes and the repair-stage trace for qualitative failure-mode analysis. The execution manifest reports model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage = 1.

Threats to validity and limitations (summary): Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and an automated paired protocol with no manual adjudication. Construct validity depends on the verifier’s modeled property set; if operators care about other properties the measured pass-rate difference will understate verifier utility. External validity is constrained by a single requested model, one deterministic validator, a synthetic task corpus limited to three task clusters, and allowed_fields restricted to {admin, mtu, vlan}. Conclusion validity is limited by the ceiling effect caused by much lower-than-assumed baseline error prevalence. The archived validator-spec artifacts enumerate the validator’s coverage and severity mapping for readers assessing applicability.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) isolating verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. With the requested model/validator pairing and a verifier-scoped synthetic corpus the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the archived two-sided binomial convention). The result documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal error prevalence is extremely low and verifier coverage is constrained, measured marginal pass-rate gains may be negligible, though verifiers can still correct rare but concrete failures (one archived corrected episode). We recommend practitioners measure baseline proposal error prevalence and align verifier coverage and generation semantics with operational priorities. All artifacts necessary to reproduce, re-run, or inspect the single corrected episode and full analysis are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic inspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads in the archive show allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not necessarily generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived two-sided exact-binomial convention for n = 1 discordant pair and must be interpreted in that context.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
